summary: Phase 5e-iv landed — read-only Lattice screen at /lattice surfacing the operator's direct web in one view. Three sections in this order: recovery cohort (M of N peers + Cohort badge + Declared date), People (handshakes with Tier P / Tier R counts, plus a Cohort badge on the cards whose peer is also in the recovery cohort), Organizations (memberships with the existing chain-walk sheet for nested orgs). Empty states route the operator back to the editing surfaces — Settings for cohort, the People tab for handshakes. Friend-of-friend transitive paths explicitly named as a future increment per the spec's 'direct list first, transitive scoring later.'

why.text: Operator's standing directive carried in this branch: 'fire up and take over on next steps knock out what you can as long as you see the line.' The Phase 5e brief's locked sequence: 5e-i (decision) → 5e-ii (Shamir primitives, DONE c8852b3) → 5e-iii-a (cohort UI, DONE 34ad1a8) → 5e-iii-b (backup v2, DONE 84ebbc2) → 5e-iv (Lattice view, this cut) → 5e-v / 5e-vi / 5e-vii (the recovery ceremony, deferred to a multi-session arc). 5e-iv is the rendering-shaped cut sized at 3-5 days in the brief; one session was enough.

outcome.notes: [P-001] LatticeScreen shipped at /lattice — three sections (Recovery cohort / People / Organizations) with read-only rendering and Cohort badge cross-reference. [P-002] HomeScreen header gains a Lattice link next to Settings; both wrap in flex gap-4 so the layout stays single-line on 375px. [P-003] App.tsx lazy-loads the screen as a separate chunk; ships at 2.12 KB gz under a 5 KB budget. [P-004] Recovery manifest's touches array + purpose updated to record the cut. [P-005] All four gates green: typecheck, lint, test (36/36), build (bundle budgets all green). [FEEDBACK→Foreman]: 5e-v / 5e-vi (recovery ceremony, initiator + responder) is the heavy interactive protocol piece — sized 1-2 weeks each in the brief — and should probably get a multi-session arc rather than a single-session knockout. The state machine has explicit verification steps with out-of-band gating that need careful UX, and the Mycelium round-trips need ack-aware honest status. Recommend brief-refresh before code lands.

uncertainty: Did not exercise the screen in a browser this session — operator field walk-through is still the highest-fidelity validation. The cross-section Cohort badge on ConnectionCard uses absolute positioning with a fixed right offset which could overlap awkwardly on long peer names on very narrow screens; the existing Tier P/R badge has the same right-anchor pattern but doesn't compose with the new Cohort badge. Worth a five-second look in DevTools at 320px width before declaring the visual unconditionally clean.

next: Phase 5e-v — recovery ceremony, initiator side. Per the brief: new-device first-run detects cloud-backup blob exists, generates a fresh local keypair, publishes a recovery request via Mycelium addressed to each cohort member's pubkey, names the new keypair in the request, asks peers to verify out-of-band before encrypting their shares. State machine work: fresh keypair generation + recovery-request envelope shape + Mycelium publish + collect-M-shares + combine + decrypt + Wallet.restore. The brief recommends brief-first for 5e-v because the state machine is real protocol work; this matches the [FEEDBACK→Foreman] note above. After 5e-v: 5e-vi (responder), 5e-vii (recovery-succession event), then Phase 5f (quorum org keys per the existing brief).
